verdict.rationale: Notte documents a DOM-understanding `observe()` primitive (and CLI `notte page observe`) that returns element IDs and selectors to act on. It also supports hybrid scripting, where deterministic steps are scripted and AI is used only when needed, and it markets 'No selectors, no maintenance.' That points to its own semantic action layer, but the pack never shows explicit act/click/type calls on natural-language-described elements, and resilience to selector or layout changes is only a marketing claim. A community comment questioning action-space reliability is skepticism, not a concrete failure, so it does not make the verdict disputed. Missing for 10: documented act/click/type primitives targeting described elements, evidence that actions survive selector and layout changes, independent hands-on corroboration.
